text:
This guidance explains how to complete the questions in the non‑tax advantaged share scheme (‘Non-Tass’) Employment Related Securities (ERS) annual end of year return. It also identifies which questions are mandatory, conditional mandatory or optional.

There have been some changes made to the end of year return headings. If you wish to create your own end of year template, you can check: (From April 2027) Non-Tax Advantaged employment related securities schemes or arrangements: guidance notes.

The current Non-Tass Employment Related Securities end of year return is version 7.

1. Who must submit an end of year return

The company secretary, or the person acting as company secretary, must submit an online end‑of‑year ERS return by 6 July following the end of the tax year.

In circumstances where the employee is employed by an Employer of Record (EoR), the EoR is responsible for submitting the returns.

An end of year return must be submitted for each registered Non-Tass ERS scheme or arrangement.

2. When to submit an end of year return or a nil return

If you operate an ERS scheme, you are required to submit an end of year ERS return, including nil returns, for every scheme registered.

If your scheme has ended and you have entered a final event date, you must submit any outstanding returns up until the date that it ended.

You do not need to submit an ERS end of year return for any events which would normally be reportable if you meet ALL the below criteria:

neither the company, nor any other company in the same group or under the same ownership, is registered for PAYE

the arrangements are not tax-advantaged schemes (that is, not Share Incentive Plan, Save As You Earn, Company Share Option Plan or Enterprise Management Incentive schemes)

the company has no obligations to operate PAYE in respect of the reportable event

the company has no obligation to operate PAYE in respect of anything else it does

Short term business visitors (STBV)

Where an employee is a STBV covered by an EP Appendix 4 arrangement, there is no requirement to report non‑tax advantaged ERS data for that employee, provided no UK Income Tax or National Insurance contributions are due.

This applies to all current, previous and future tax years.

The reporting requirement still applies where UK Income Tax or National Insurance contributions would be due as a result of the application of Chapter 5B of Part 2 ITEPA 2003. For example, if an employee has worked in the UK and overseas or been UK resident previously.

Where an employee is a STBV covered by an EP Appendix 8 arrangement, the ERS reporting obligation remains.

3. Completing and uploading your end of year return

3.1 Checking your end of year return

You can use the Employment related securities (ERS) checking service to check your end of year return.

The service:

shows where formatting errors occur which will prevent your end of year return being submitted successfully

can be used as often as needed

helps you correct errors early, making submission easier

You can also access the checking service through ‘View my schemes and arrangements’ on the online ERS service

4. General guidance on valuations

All values must be entered in pounds sterling to 4 decimal places.

Where necessary:

round up figures ending in 5 or more

round down figures ending in 4 or less

If a value is quoted in another currency, use a reputable currency converter to convert it to pounds sterling.

You do not need to formally agree valuations of shares and securities with HMRC.

Where shares are not listed on a recognised stock exchange, you may have asked HMRC for a valuation. If a valuation was agreed with HMRC:

enter the valuation reference number on the end of year return

if the reference is prefixed with Company Reference Number (CRN), do not enter those letters

If no valuation was agreed, you must retain records showing how the valuation was reasonably determined.

4.1 Actual Market Value (AMV)

AMV is the value of a share or security after taking account of:

restrictions

risk of forfeiture

4.2 Unrestricted Market Value (UMV)

UMV is the value of a share or security ignoring:

restrictions

risk of forfeiture

4.3 Recognised stock exchanges

For more information about recognised stock exchanges read Recognised stock exchanges: definition, legislation and tables.

AIM (Alternative Investment Market) and PISCES (Private Intermittent Securities and Capital Exchange System) are not recognised stock exchanges for these purposes.

5. General guidance on completing the end of year return

5.1 Mandatory, conditional mandatory, and optional fields

Mandatory — a response is always required regardless of any other information provided.

Conditional Mandatory — a response is only required if you have provided a response to a mandatory question.

For example, on the Non-Tass end of year return where it asks if the event is in relation to a disclosable tax avoidance scheme and the answer is yes, then the next question will require a response.

Optional — this field can be left blank but should be completed if you know the information requested.

If a conditional mandatory, or optional field does not require a response, leave it blank.

Do not enter:

‘N/A’

‘not applicable’

Doing so will cause your end of year return to be rejected.

5.2 Yes and no answers

The following formats are accepted:

Yes, yes, YES

No, no, NO

6. Common worksheet fields

The following fields appear on most non‑tax advantaged worksheets. Please refer back to this section when completing the common field questions.

6.1 Is the event in relation to a disclosable tax avoidance scheme.

Read the rules about DOTAS.

Enter yes or no.

This field is mandatory.

If yes, enter the eight-digit Scheme Reference Number (SRN).

If you have disclosed a tax avoidance scheme under the DOTAS rules, HMRC will have given you an 8 digit-long Scheme Reference Number (SRN).

Enter this number.

This field is conditional mandatory.

6.2 Employing company

Enter the details of the company that employs the employee who was awarded or acquired the ERS.

Refer to the technical note for mandatory fields.

6.3 Employee first name

This is the employee’s first name.

This field is mandatory.

6.4 Employee second name (optional).

If the employee has a second name, then enter in this column.

This field is optional.

6.5 Employee last name

This is the employee’s last name.

This field is mandatory.

6.6 National Insurance number

Enter in the correct format, for example, QQ123456C

Most individuals included on an ERS end of year return will have a National Insurance number.

In exceptional cases, use an alternative reference instead.

This reference must:

only be used on the ERS end of year return

not be used in any other HMRC correspondence

not be given to the individual

Where there are exceptional circumstances, the required format for the alternative ERS reference will be a total of 9 characters. This will be 2 letters, 6 numbers and one letter consisting of:

TN – to indicate an ERS reference

Employee Date of Birth in format DDMMYY (for example, 080403) ― this data will enable HMRC to trace the individual

No National Insurance number Reason Identifier (X, Y or Z) ― this is to identify the reason why an individual does not have a National Insurance number

X ― Under 16 years old

Y ― Applied for a National Insurance number and is waiting to receive it

Z — Never paid National Insurance contributions as they have not been liable to UK National Insurance contributions ― for example, they’re not resident in the UK or are an ‘intra-company worker’ on transfer to work in the UK

This field is mandatory.

6.7 Company Registration Number (CRN)

This is the number issued by Companies House to UK registered companies. If the company is not UK registered or does not have this number, then do not make any entry in this column.

This field is optional.

6.8 Recognised stock exchange

For more information, go to Recognised stock exchanges .

AIM and PISCES are not recognised stock exchanges for these purposes.

6.9 Has a NICs election or agreement been operated?

This is when the employer and the employee agree or jointly elect for the employee to meet the employer’s liability to pay secondary National Insurance contributions on certain types of share awards and share options gains. The employee can then get a deduction equal to the amount of secondary or employers’ National Insurance contributions transferred when working out the amount chargeable to Income Tax. ‘Operated’ means when the secondary or employers’ National Insurance contributions is recovered under the terms of election or agreement already made between the employer and the employee.

This field is mandatory.

6.10 Was PAYE operated?

Enter ‘yes’ or ‘no’ in this field.

If shares are readily convertible into cash and a reportable event is taxable such as an acquisition of the shares, then PAYE should have been operated to collect any Income Tax and NICs due.

There are exceptions, for example, following death (check ERSM20270 - Employment-related securities and options: exclusions: deaths), or after an employee leaves and the 7-year rule applies (check ERSM20280 - Employment-related securities and options: exclusions: 7 year rule).

This field is mandatory.

6.11 Was any adjustment made for amounts subject to apportionment for residence or duties outside the UK?

Where the employee is an ‘internationally mobile employee’ (IME), the income derived from the securities may be apportioned if the required conditions are met. The rules for IMEs will identify any foreign securities income which is either not chargeable to UK Income Tax or taxable only when remitted to the UK. Guidance on the ERS rules for IMEs can be found at ERSM162000 - International from 6 April 2015 and ERSM165000 - International from 6 April 2025.

For further information regarding non-UK domiciled individuals see UK tax residence guidance.

This field is mandatory.

7. Worksheet specific guidance

The following sections explain when to use each worksheet and how to complete its questions.

Use a separate row for each individual unless stated otherwise.

(All worksheet definitions, questions, routing rules, thresholds, examples and calculations remain unchanged and are presented in a clearer sequence below.)

Please note when completing the end of year return if you leave 10 or more consecutive rows blank with no data populated, it will be assumed that there is no further information contained below these blank rows within the sheet. Therefore, it is important you do not leave blank rows between the rows of data you are reporting. Note the system will continue to check for information on subsequent sheets within the same end of year return.

8. Non‑TASS_Grants_V7_worksheet

Use this worksheet to tell HMRC about any employment related securities options granted in the tax year.

Include all types of securities options including nil cost options. Reporting of Restricted Stock Units (RSUs) will depend on how these are structured. Whether the RSUs are considered securities options or not will determine on which worksheet these should be reported.

For more information read securities options guidance.

8.1 Question 1: Date of grant

Enter the date the ERS options were granted to the employees.

Use the format yyyy‑mm‑dd (for example: 2023‑10‑31).

The date of grant will be on the option certificate, and it must fall within the tax year covered by this return.

Options granted on the same date can be reported in one row, provided the Unrestricted Market Value (UMV) of the security is the same for all options granted on that date.

This field is mandatory.

8.2 Question 2: Number of employees granted options

Enter the total number of employees who were granted ERS options on this grant date.

This field is optional.

8.3 Question 3: Unrestricted market value of a security at date of grant

Enter the value in pounds to 4 decimal places (for example, 10.1234).

This is not the exercise, grant or strike price, which may or may not be the same as the UMV at grant.

This field is optional.

8.4 Question 4: Number of securities over which options were granted

Enter the number to 2 decimal places (for example, 100.00).

Enter the total number of securities under ERS options granted to employees on this grant date.

This field is optional.

9 Non‑TASS_Options_V7 worksheet

Use this worksheet to tell HMRC about options exercised, released, assigned, cancelled or lapsed in the tax year.

Use this worksheet to also report securities acquired from a securities option without exercising it. Do not fill in this sheet if options are released, assigned, cancelled or lapse for nil consideration.

Use a different row to report each individual’s details.

9.1 Question 1: Date of event

Enter the date of the event in the correct format (yyyy‑mm‑dd), for example, 2023-10-31.

The date of event is the date the ERS options were exercised, released, assigned, cancelled or lapsed.

This field is mandatory.

9.2 Questions 2 to 7

See common fields guidance under section 6.

9.3 Question 8: PAYE reference of employing company

Enter the PAYE reference number of the company that employs the employee.

The employing company is the organisation with the PAYE obligation.

This field is mandatory.

9.4 Question 9: Date of grant of option subject to the reportable event

Enter the date in the format yyyy‑mm‑dd. (for example, 2023‑10‑31)

This is the date the ERS options were granted to the employees. This date will be shown on the option certificate or agreement.

This field is mandatory.

9.5 Questions 10 to 19: Grantor or employing company details, CRN, CT Ref, PAYE Ref

The grantor company is the organisation that decided which employees will be awarded options.

If options were granted by:

a partnership

a sole trader

an individual

Enter their details here. You do not need to enter a Company Registration Number (CRN), Corporation Tax reference or PAYE reference if they do not have one.

Mandatory questions in this section:

Grantor company name (Q10)

Grantor company address line 1 (Q11)

All the remaining questions in this section are Optional.

9.6 Questions 20 to 29: Company whose securities are under option

Enter details of the company whose securities are under option.

Scheme rules and other documents relating to the award of the option will show the details of the company.

Mandatory questions in this section:

Name of the company whose securities under option (Q20)

Company whose securities under option - address line 1 (Q21)

All the remaining questions in this section are optional.

9.7 Question 30: Were the options exercised?

Enter yes or no.

Enter:

‘yes’ if the employee exercised the option. Go to question 31.

‘no’ if the option was not exercised, but another event needs to be reported in relation to that option. Go to question 38.

This field is optional.

9.8 Question 31: Total number of securities employee entitled to on exercise of the option before any cashless exercise or other adjustment

Enter the number to 2 decimal places (for example: 100.00).

Enter the gross number of securities the employee was entitled to acquire from this exercise, vesting or event, before any:

cashless exercise

other adjustment, including net settlement

For example, an employee has an option to acquire 1,000 shares. On exercise, 420 shares are either:

immediately sold by the employee to pay the Income Tax and National Insurance contributions liability under ‘sell to cover’ arrangements

retained by the company under a net settlement arrangement to pay the tax and National Insurance contributions liability, or

used to account for another adjustment, including a net settlement for the exercise price

In all these scenarios, the value entered for Question 31 is 1,000.00.

This field is optional.

9.9 Question 32: If consideration was given for the securities, the amount given per security.

Enter the value in pounds to 4 decimal places (for example, 10.1234)

Only enter any consideration paid by the employee per security and not the total to acquire the security. This will most commonly be the exercise price.

The exercise price can also be referred to as grant or strike price.

This field is optional.

9.10 Question 33: If securities were acquired, Market Value of a security on the date of acquisition.

Enter the value in pounds to 4 decimal places (for example, 10.1234)

This field is optional.

9.11 Question 34: If shares were acquired, are the shares listed on a recognised stock exchange?

Enter yes or no.

If yes, go to Question 37.

If no, go to Question 35.

For more information about recognised stock exchange read Recognised stock exchanges: definition, legislation and tables.

AIM and PISCES are not recognised stock exchanges for these purposes.

This field is optional.

9.12 Question 35: If shares were not listed on a recognised stock exchange, was valuation agreed with HMRC?

Enter yes or no.

Only complete this if the shares were not listed on a recognised stock exchange.

If yes, go to Question 36.

If no, go to Question 37.

This field is optional.

9.13 Question 36: If yes, enter the HMRC valuation reference given

Enter the HMRC valuation reference, this will be on the valuation letter sent to you from the Shares and Assets Valuation office.

This will normally be your Company Reference Number (CRN).

Enter the full reference including letters and number.

If it starts with 3 letters, include numbers only.

This field is conditional mandatory.

9.14 Question 37: If the shares were acquired, total deductible amount excluding any consideration given for the securities

Enter the value in pounds sterling to 4 decimal places (for example, 10.1234)

This is the total amount of:

any amount paid for the grant of the option

any expenses incurred for the acquisition of the securities

Do not include:

the exercise (grant or strike) price

any expenses connected with the sale or disposal of the securities

Income Tax

employer National Insurance contributions the employee may have agreed to pay under a joint agreement or election

This field is optional.

9.15 Question 38: If securities were not acquired, was money or value received on the release, assignment, cancellation or lapse of the option?

Enter yes or no.

If yes, go to Question 39.

If no, no further information is required for this event.

This field is optional.

9.16 Question 39: If yes, amount of money or value received.

Enter the value in pounds to 4 decimal places (for example, 10.1234)

Enter:

the amount of money or money’s worth received by the individual employee or anyone else for the ERS options released (including exchanges), cancelled or lapsed.

the amount of the Income Tax and National Insurance contributions that was paid through net settlement.

For example, where the employee does not acquire all the shares subject to the option and instead the employer makes a corresponding cash payment under a net settlement arrangement to pay the employee’s Income Tax and National Insurance contributions liability, the Income Tax and National Insurance contributions values paid via a net settlement arrangement should be entered here.

If there is a net settlement to cover the exercise price of an option, this should not be reported at questions 38 or 39.

This field is optional.

9.17 Question 40 to 42:

See common fields guidance in section 6.

10 Non‑TASS_Acquisition_V7 worksheet

Use this worksheet to tell HMRC about acquisitions of securities but not through securities options in the tax year.

You would report acquisitions by employees of securities with or without any restrictions attached to them, securities that have a right to convert to other securities and shares awarded to employees under an Employee Shareholder Agreement.

Use a different row to report each employee’s details.

10.1 Question 1: Date of event

Enter the date in the correct format (yyyy-mm-dd) (for example, 2023‑10‑31)

This is the date the employee was awarded or acquired the securities.

This field is mandatory.

10.2 Questions 2 to 7

See common fields guidance in section 6.

10.3 Question 8: PAYE reference of employing company

Enter the PAYE reference number of the company that employs the employee.

The employing company should be the company with the PAYE obligation.

This field is mandatory.

10.4 Questions 9 to 17: Company whose securities acquired

Enter details of the company whose securities were acquired.

This may be the same as the employing company.

Mandatory questions in this section:

Name of the company whose securities acquired (Q9)

Company whose securities acquired- address line 1 (Q10)

The remaining questions in this section are optional.

10. 5 Question 18: PAYE reference of company whose securities were acquired

If the company whose securities were acquired has a PAYE reference, enter it here.

This field is optional.

10.6 Question 19: Description of security

Enter a number only from 1 to 9.

Do not enter text.

Select the most accurate description:

Shares.

Rights under contracts of insurance.

Debentures, loan stock, bonds or other debt instruments’

Warrants.

Certificates or other instruments conferring rights in securities.

Units in a collective investment scheme.

Options and futures.

Rights under contracts for differences.

Alternative finance arrangements.

This field is mandatory.

10.7 Question 20: If the securities are not shares enter ‘no’ and go to question 24. If the securities are shares, are they part of the largest class of shares in the company?

Enter yes or no.

Some companies create different classes of ordinary share, for example ’A’ and ‘B’ ordinary shares. The largest class of share is the class of shares with entitlement to the largest proportion of value (£) on a winding-up.

If you only have one class of shares, enter ‘yes’.

If you have more than one class of share and all classes of shares are equal in value enter ‘yes’.

This field is mandatory.

10.8 Question 21: If the securities are shares, are they listed on a recognised stock exchange?

Enter yes or no.

If yes, go to Question 24.

If no, go to Question 22.

This field is conditional mandatory.

10.9 Question 22: If the shares were not listed on a recognised stock exchange, was a valuation agreed with HMRC?

Enter yes or no.

Only complete this question if the shares were not listed on a recognised stock exchange.

If yes, go to Question 23.

If no, go to Question 24.

This field is conditional mandatory.

10.10 Question 23: If yes, enter the HMRC valuation reference given

The HMRC valuation reference will be on the valuation letter sent to you from the Shares and Assets Valuation office.

The reference given will normally be your Company Reference Number (CRN).

Enter the full reference including the letters and numbers.

If the beginning of your reference has 3 letters, only include the numbers.

This field is conditional mandatory.

10.11 Question 24: Number of securities acquired

Enter the number to 2 decimal places (for example: 100.00)

Enter the total number, and not the value, of the gross securities to which the employee was entitled before any net settlement or other adjustment.

This field is optional.

10.12 Question 25: Security type.

Enter a number from 1 to 3.

If restricted, enter 1 and go to Question 26.

If unrestricted, enter 2 and go to Question 29.

If convertible, enter 3 and go to Question 32.

If restricted and convertible, enter 1 and answer Questions 26 to 40.

1. Restricted securities (or an interest in securities)

Securities are restricted if their market value at the date of acquisition is less than it would otherwise be because:

there is a restriction on the rights including the rights to keep or sell the securities

a disadvantage could arise if the rights to the securities were exercised, including disadvantages to do with keeping or selling of the securities

a transfer, reversion or forfeiture will occur if certain circumstances arise or do not arise

They are not restricted if they must be sold or transferred if employment ends because of misconduct.

2. Unrestricted securities

Securities that do not have any restrictions that could affect market value.

3. Convertible securities

Securities are convertible If:

the holder can convert them into securities of a different description (even if this is dependent on certain conditions being met)

the holder may be granted the right to convert some time in the future by contract, agreement, arrangement, condition or under the Articles of Association of the company whose securities are being issued

a contract, agreement, arrangement or condition allows the securities to be converted by someone other than the person holding them

This field is mandatory.

10.13 Question 26: If restricted, nature of restriction.

Enter a number from 1 to 3.

If more than one applies, choose the first relevant option:

Forfeiture — where the holder of the securities or interest in the securities will no longer have any beneficial interest in them.

Restriction on retention or disposal — this could include restrictions on voting or dividends, or a rule which means the holder cannot sell the securities for a fixed period.

Potential disadvantage — this could be any rule that would mean the employee would suffer a disadvantage if the securities were sold. For example, a rule which meant an employee would have to leave their employment if the shares were sold.

This field is conditional mandatory.

10.14 Question 27: If restricted, length of time of restriction in years.

Enter the time in years.

If the time is less than a whole year, enter as a decimal fraction to 1 decimal place, for example 0.6.

Enter 999 if the length of restriction is conditional, variable or has not been determined.

This field is optional.

10.15 Question 28: If restricted, actual market value per security at date of acquisition.

Enter the value in pounds to 4 decimal places. (for example: 10.1234)

Do not complete this field if a section 431 election has been made to disregard all the restrictions.

This field is optional.

10.16 Question 29: Unrestricted market value per security at date of acquisition.

Enter the value in pounds to 4 decimal places (for example, 10.1234).

Enter UMV per security.

This field is optional.

10.17 Question 30: If restricted, has an election been operated to disregard restrictions?

Enter yes or no.

Under the employment related securities tax legislation, it is possible for an employer and employee to enter into a Section 431 or 430 election. The effect of a section 431 election is to disregard all or some restrictions depending on how it is made.

This field is conditional mandatory.

10.18 Question 31: If an election has been operated to disregard restrictions, have all or some been disregarded?

Enter all or some.

Under the employment related securities tax legislation, an employer and employee may enter into a Section 431 or 430 election. A section 431 election can be made to disregard all restrictions or only some restrictions, depending on how the election is structured.

Select “all” or “some” based on the specific type of election that was made.

This field is conditional mandatory.

10.19 Question 32: If convertible, market value per security ignoring conversion rights.

Enter the value per security in pounds to 4 decimal places. (for example: 10.1234).

Enter the market value of the securities acquired as if they were not convertible.

This field is optional.

10.20 Question 33: Total price paid for the securities

Enter the total price paid in pounds to 4 decimal places (for example: 10.1234).

If the securities were acquired at no cost (without any payment for them) enter 0.0000.

If you are reporting a share for share exchange event, then you would enter the total value of the shares given up.

This field is optional.

10.21 Question 34: Was the price paid in pounds sterling?

Enter yes or no.

If you entered 0.0000 in Question 33, enter ‘no’.

This field is mandatory.

10.22 Question 35: Was there an artificial reduction in value on acquisition?

Enter yes or no.

If yes, go to question 36.

If no, go to question 37.

Only enter yes if there were artificial reductions (not discounts) in the market value of securities arising from non-commercial actions. Checkexamples in: ERSM50030 - Securities with Artificially Depressed Value.

Non-commercial actions include any reduction made:

for anything other than a genuine commercial purpose

as part of a scheme or arrangement designed to avoid tax or National Insurance contributions

because of any transaction between companies within a group on preferential terms that would not have been made if the companies were at arm’s length

This field is mandatory.

10.23 Question 36: If there was an artificial reduction in value, nature of the artificial reduction.

Only complete this if you answered ‘yes’ to Question 35.

Enter a number from 1 to 3:

Non-commercial transaction.

Scheme or arrangement designed to avoid tax or National Insurance.

Inter- company transaction on a non-arm’s length basis.

This field is conditional mandatory.

10.24 Question 37: Were shares acquired under an employee shareholder arrangement?

Enter yes or no.

You should only make an entry in this column if shares were acquired under an Employee Shareholder agreement as defined in Section 205A of the Employment Rights Act 1996.

An employee shareholder is someone who works under an employee shareholder employment contract. Employees with an employee shareholder agreement have different employment rights to other employees.

As part of the agreement employee shareholders must be given shares worth at least £2000 on receipt.

This field is mandatory.

10.25 Question 38: If shares were acquired under an employee shareholder arrangement, was the total actual market value (AMV) of shares £2,000 or more?

Enter yes or no.

Enter yes if the AMV of the shares acquired under an employee shareholder arrangement is £2,000 or more.

This field is conditional mandatory.

10.26 Question 39 and 40

See common fields guidance in section 6.

11 Non‑TASS_RestrictedSecurities_V7 worksheet

Use this worksheet to tell HMRC details of chargeable events after acquisition of restricted securities.

Securities are considered restricted securities if their market value is reduced because of restrictions, such as those relating to transfer, reversion or forfeiture. The chargeable amount is calculated using a prescribed formula.

You can get a spreadsheet to help you determine this amount by emailing, shareschemes@hmrc.gov.uk.

When chargeable events arise

A chargeable event arises if:

the securities stop being subject to forfeiture (conditional)

any restriction is changed or removed from the securities by any means, including if any time restrictions have lapsed

the securities are sold to an unconnected person while still restricted

Use a separate row for each individual.

11.1 Question 1: Date of event

Enter the date in the correct format (yyyy-mm-dd), for example: 2023‑10‑31.

Enter date of reportable events occurring after acquisition of restricted securities.

This field is mandatory.

11.2 Questions 2 to 7

See common fields guidance in section 6.

11.3 Question 8: PAYE reference of employing company

Enter the PAYE reference number of the company that employs the employee.

The employing company should be the company with the PAYE obligation.

This field is mandatory.

11.4 Question 9: Date securities originally acquired.

Enter the date in the format (yyyy‑mm‑dd), for example: 2023‑10‑31.

This is the date when the restricted securities on which you are now reporting an event were originally acquired.

This field is mandatory.

11.5 Question 10: Number of securities originally acquired

Enter the number of securities to 2 decimal places (for example: 100.00).

Enter the number, not the value, of restricted securities originally acquired.

This field is optional.

11.6 Question 11: For disposals or lifting of restrictions, total chargeable amount.

Enter the amount in pounds to 4 decimal places (for example: 10.1234).

Enter the total amount chargeable when restrictions on securities are lifted or there is a disposal of restricted securities.

For the vesting of restricted securities, the chargeable amount in box 11 should be based on the value of the gross number of shares subject to the chargeable event.

This applies even if some shares are disposed of at the time to cover Income Tax and National Insurance contributions.

This field is optional.

11.7 Question 12: For lifting of restrictions, are the shares listed on a recognised stock exchange?

Enter yes or no.

If yes, go to question 15.

If no, go to question 13.

This field is conditional mandatory.

11.8 Question 13: If the shares were not listed on a recognised stock exchange, was a valuation agreed with HMRC?

Enter yes or no.

Only complete this question if the shares were not listed on a recognised stock exchange.

If yes, go to question 14.

If no, go to question 15.

This field is conditional mandatory.

11.9 Question 14: If yes, enter the HMRC valuation reference given.

Enter the HMRC valuation reference, this will be on the valuation letter sent to you from the Shares and Assets Valuation office. The reference given will normally be your Company Reference Number (CRN).

Enter the full reference including the letters and numbers.

If it begins with 3 letters, enter numbers only.

This field is conditional mandatory.

11.10 Question 15: For variations, date of variation.

Enter the date in the format (yyyy‑mm‑dd) for example: 2023‑10‑31.

Enter the date when there has been an increase in value of the securities because of alteration in the rights or any restrictions attached to them or other shares in the company.

Do not complete this column in connection with the variation if:

all of the shares of the same class are similarly restricted

the majority of the shares are held by persons other than employees or directors

employees or directors control the company by virtue of their holdings of that class of shares

the company is a subsidiary and has only one class of shares

This field is conditional mandatory.

11.11 Question 16: For variations, Actual Market Value (AMV) per security directly before variation.

Enter the value in pounds to 4 decimal places (for example, 10.1234).

This field is optional.

11.12 Question 17: For variations, Actual Market Value (AMV) per security directly after variation.

Enter the value in pounds to 4 decimal places (for example: 10.1234).

This field is optional.

11.13 Questions 18 to 20

See common fields guidance in section 6.

12 Non‑TASS_Other_Benefits_V7 worksheet

You must fill in this sheet if an employee, or a person connected with an employee, has received a benefit in connection with employment-related securities, that is not otherwise chargeable to Income Tax.

The ‘not otherwise chargeable’ exemption does not apply in cases involving avoidance of Income Tax or National Insurance contributions. Use this sheet to tell HMRC about any benefit received after the acquisition in the tax year. Benefits include a whole range of things. For more information read Post Acquisition Benefits from Securities.

Use a separate row for each individual.

Enter the date in the format (yyyy‑mm‑dd) for example: 2023‑10‑31.

This is the date when the restricted securities on which you are now reporting an event were originally acquired.

Enter the amount or market value of the benefit received, not the market value of the securities themselves.

13 Non‑TASS_Convertible_V7 worksheet

Use this worksheet to tell HMRC about any benefit or chargeable amount received from convertible securities in the tax year. Only complete this sheet if an employee has acquired employment-related securities that carry an immediate or potential entitlement to be converted into securities of a different description.

Do not fill in this sheet if:

all the shares of the same class are convertible securities

all the shares of the same class are affected by an event similar to the chargeable event, and either immediately before the chargeable event

employees hold the majority of the company’s shares of that class and consequently can control the company

associated companies, employees and their relatives do not hold the majority of the company’s shares of the same class as those shares acquired

the avoidance of Income Tax and National Insurance contributions was not the main purpose, or one of the main purposes, of the arrangements under which the right or opportunity to acquire the employment-related securities was made available.

13.1 Question 1: Date of event

14 Non‑TASS_Notional_V7 worksheet

Use this worksheet to tell HMRC about the amount of notional loan outstanding immediately before discharge for each relevant person in the tax year.

You must fill in this sheet where a notional loan is treated as discharged, creating a taxable amount. This may occur when the employment related securities are disposed of to someone other than to a connected person, or an outstanding liability to pay for the securities is released.

When a notional loan is discharged, the resulting amount is treated as employment income and is subject to Income Tax.

Where the securities are readily convertible assets, the amount is subject to Income Tax and National Insurance contributions and must be accounted for through PAYE.

Use a separate row for each individual.

14.1 Question 1: Date of event

Enter the date in the correct format (yyyy-mm-dd). For example: 2023‑10‑31.

Enter the date the notional loan was treated as discharged.

This field is mandatory.

14.2 Questions 2 to 7

See common fields guidance in section 6.

14.3 Question 8: PAYE reference of employing company

Enter the PAYE reference number of the company that employs the employee.

The employing company should be the company with the PAYE obligation.

This field is mandatory.

14.4 Question 9: Date securities were originally acquired

Enter the date in the correct format (yyyy‑mm‑dd). For example: 2023‑10‑31.

Enter the date the securities were originally acquired, even if you are reporting a later event.

This field is mandatory.

14.5 Question 10: Number of securities originally acquired

Enter the number of securities to 2 decimal places. For example: 100.00.

Enter the number, not the value, of securities originally acquired on which the discharge of the notional loan occurred.

This field is optional.

14.6 Question 11: Amount of notional loan discharged

Enter the value in pounds sterling to 4 decimal places. For example: 10.1234.

Enter the amount of the notional loan outstanding immediately before discharge.

This field is optional.

15 Non‑TASS_Enhancement_V7 worksheet

You must use this worksheet to tell HMRC about any securities artificially enhanced.

For example, the market value of an employee’s employment related securities is increased by more than 10% by non-commercial actions in a relevant period. The relevant period runs from the date securities are acquired to the earlier of the date of disposal or 5 April of the tax year for this reportable event. The date of the taxable event will be 5 April or the date the securities were disposed of, if earlier.

Enter the date in the correct format (yyyy-mm-dd). For example: 2023‑10‑31.

16 Non‑TASS_Sold_V7 worksheet

Use this worksheet to tell HMRC about securities sold for more than their market value for each relevant person in the tax year.

This worksheet should be completed if the employee, or a person connected with the employee, has disposed of employment related securities on or after the 6 April for more than their market value at the time of disposal.

In these circumstances, the amount treated as employment income is the consideration received on disposal, less the market value of the securities at disposal, and any allowable expenses.
